memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Have them make an ark of acacia wood — two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. Overlay it with pure gold, both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it." - Exodus 25:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ark of the covenant is the first item God describes — the most sacred object in Israel's worship. And notice the detail: it was overlaid with pure gold both inside and out. The outside anyone could see. The inside no one would ever look at. Yet God asked for gold there too.

That small instruction carries a big truth. God cares about what is hidden as much as what is displayed. The parts of our lives that no one inspects — our private thoughts, our unseen motives, the way we behave when no one is watching — matter deeply to Him. Integrity means being the same on the inside as we appear on the outside, gold all the way through.

Jesus reserved His sharpest words for those who polished the outside while leaving the inside unattended, calling them whitewashed tombs, beautiful outwardly but decaying within (Matt 23:27-28). God is not interested in a gilded surface over a hollow heart. And here is the grace: we cannot make our own insides golden. But God can. He works from the inside out, transforming us by renewing our minds (Rom 12:2) until what is hidden matches what is seen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is there a gap between the person others see and the person I actually am?
What hidden area of my life is God inviting me to let Him make golden?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see what no one else does. Make me the same within as I appear without, and do Your transforming work in the hidden places of my heart. Amen.
